import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

/-- A simple graph has a $K_t$ minor if it has $t$ pairwise disjoint nonempty connected
branch sets, with an edge between every two distinct branch sets. -/
def HasCliqueMinor {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : Fin t → Set V,
    (∀ i, (G.induce (branch i)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (branch i) (branch j)) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∃ u ∈ branch i, ∃ v ∈ branch j, G.Adj u v)

/--
The Hadwiger conjecture: for every finite loopless simple graph $G$ and every positive integer
$t$, if $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 :
    ∀ (V : Type) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ),
      0 < t → ¬ HasCliqueMinor G t → G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the terse list-page entry using the linked Wikipedia article as: for every finite simple graph G and every positive natural number t, absence of a K_t minor implies χ(G) < t.
Represented finite loopless undirected graphs by Mathlib's `SimpleGraph V` with a `[Finite V]` instance; `SimpleGraph` enforces symmetry and irreflexivity, hence looplessness.

Represented a K_t minor by the standard equivalent branch-set characterization: t pairwise disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets, with an edge joining every pair of distinct branch sets. Connectivity is expressed by connectivity of each induced graph.
Kept the source's restriction `0 < t`. Under the branch-set definition every graph has a K_0 minor via the empty family, but the explicit positive range records Wikipedia's intended domain.
Stated the conclusion directly as the strict inequality `G.chromaticNumber < t`; Mathlib coerces t into its extended-natural-valued chromatic number.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has simple-graph induced subgraphs, connectivity, adjacency, graph homomorphisms/embeddings, and a matroid `IsMinor`, but no simple-graph edge-contraction or graph-minor definition. The new predicate combines the existing induced-connectivity and adjacency primitives through the standard branch-set characterization.
new_definitions.name: HadwigerConjecture2.HasCliqueMinor
new_definitions.why_needed: The conjecture requires expressing that a simple graph contains a complete graph minor, but Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no graph-minor relation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a graph to its clique minors:
if a finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then $\chi(G) < t$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- H. Hadwiger, *Über eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe*, Vierteljschr. Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 88 (1943), 133–142.
- [N. Robertson, P. Seymour, R. Thomas, *Hadwiger's conjecture for $K_6$-free graphs*, Combinatorica 13 (1993), 279–361.](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01202354)
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

open SimpleGraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/--
`IsMinor H G` means that the graph `H` (on the vertex type `W`) is a *minor* of the graph `G`
(on the vertex type `V`).

We use the standard "minor model" (branch set) description: there is a family of vertex sets
`φ w ⊆ V` (`w : W`), the *branch sets*, which are pairwise disjoint, nonempty and connected
in `G`, such that whenever `w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H` some vertex of `φ w₁` is adjacent
in `G` to some vertex of `φ w₂`. Contracting each branch set to a single vertex and deleting all
remaining vertices and any superfluous edges yields `H`, so this is exactly the notion of a minor
obtained from `G` by deleting vertices, deleting edges and contracting edges.
(Nonemptiness of each branch set is part of `SimpleGraph.Connected`.)
-/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : W → Set V,
    (∀ w, (G.induce (φ w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (φ w₁) (φ w₂)) ∧
    ∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ φ w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ φ w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/-- The graph with no vertices (in particular $K_0$) is a minor of every graph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_of_isEmpty [IsEmpty W] (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor H G :=
  ⟨fun w => isEmptyElim w, fun w => isEmptyElim w, fun w => isEmptyElim w, fun w => isEmptyElim w⟩

/-- $K_1$ is a minor of `G` if and only if `G` has a vertex. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_top_fin_one_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 1)) G ↔ Nonempty V := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨φ, hconn, -, -⟩
    obtain ⟨⟨v, -⟩⟩ := (hconn 0).nonempty
    exact ⟨v⟩
  · rintro ⟨v⟩
    refine ⟨fun _ => {v}, fun _ => ?_, fun i j hij => absurd (Subsingleton.elim i j) hij,
      fun i j hij => absurd (Subsingleton.elim i j) hij.ne⟩
    haveI : Nonempty ↥({v} : Set V) := ⟨⟨v, rfl⟩⟩
    exact Connected.of_subsingleton

/-- $K_2$ is not a minor of an edgeless graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isMinor_top_fin_two_bot :
    ¬ IsMinor (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  rintro ⟨φ, -, -, hadj⟩
  obtain ⟨v₁, -, v₂, -, h⟩ := hadj 0 1 (by decide)
  exact h

/--
**Hadwiger's conjecture.**
Let $G$ be a finite loopless graph (here: a finite simple graph) and let $t$ be a positive
integer. If $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.

Equivalently, if every proper colouring of $G$ uses at least $k$ colours, then $G$ contains $k$
pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs, each pair of which is joined by an edge; contracting
these subgraphs produces $K_k$ as a minor of $G$. In algebraic form, $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where
$h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$ (the largest $k$ such that $K_k$ is a minor of $G$).

The conjecture is known for $t \le 6$ and open for every $t > 6$. The case $t = 0$ is not
excluded here because it is vacuous: $K_0$ is a minor of every graph
(`HadwigerConjecture2.isMinor_of_isEmpty`), so the hypothesis cannot hold.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (h : ¬ IsMinor (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) G) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

/--
Hadwiger's conjecture holds for $t \le 6$: the cases $t \le 4$ are due to Hadwiger (1943),
the case $t = 5$ is equivalent to the four colour theorem (Wagner, 1937), and the case $t = 6$
was proved by Robertson, Seymour and Thomas (1993), using the four colour theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2.le_six [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ 6)
    (h : ¬ IsMinor (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) G) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2

modeling_decisions: The list entry is terse; the precise formulation was taken from the article lede: "if G is loopless and has no K_t minor then χ(G) < t". Formalized as ¬ IsMinor (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) G → G.chromaticNumber < (t : ℕ∞).

new_definitions.why_needed: The conjecture is about K_t minors and neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib defines graph minors for `SimpleGraph` (checked with rg: only `Matroid.IsMinor` exists, and a comment in Mathlib/Combinatorics/Graph/Basic.lean says minors are future work). `IsMinor H G` is the standard minor-model definition: a family of branch sets φ : W → Set V, each connected in G (hence nonempty), pairwise disjoint, and for every edge w₁w₂ of H some G-edge joins φ w₁ to φ w₂. hadwiger_conjecture_2.why: Stated as: for every finite simple graph G (a `SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]`, which is automatically loopless) and every t : ℕ, if K_t = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin t)) is not a minor of G then G.chromaticNumber < t (in ℕ∞). /-- A simple graph `G` has a complete graph on `t` vertices as a minor if it has `t`
pairwise disjoint connected branch sets, with an edge between every pair of branch sets. -/
def HasCompleteMinor {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ branchSet : Fin t → Set V,
    (∀ i, (G.induce (branchSet i)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (branchSet i) (branchSet j)) ∧
    Pairwise fun i j ↦ ∃ v ∈ branchSet i, ∃ w ∈ branchSet j, G.Adj v w

-- Every graph has the empty complete graph as a minor.
example {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : HasCompleteMinor G 0 := by
  simp [HasCompleteMinor]

/--
**Hadwiger conjecture.** For every finite loopless simple graph `G` and every positive
integer $t$, if `G` has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a graph to its clique minors: if a
finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then $\chi(G) < t$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Ha43] Hadwiger, Hugo (1943), "Über eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe",
  *Vierteljschr. Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich* 88, pp. 133--143.
* [RST93] Robertson, Neil; Seymour, Paul; Thomas, Robin (1993), "Hadwiger's conjecture for
  $K_6$-free graphs", *Combinatorica* 13 (3), pp. 279--361.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

variable {V W : Type*}

/--
`IsMinor H G` means that the simple graph `H` is a *minor* of the simple graph `G`.

We use the standard "model" (branch set) formulation: there is a family of pairwise disjoint
vertex sets `B w ⊆ V` (one for each vertex `w` of `H`), each of which is nonempty and induces a
connected subgraph of `G`, such that for every edge `w₁w₂` of `H` there is an edge of `G`
between `B w₁` and `B w₂`. Contracting each branch set `B w` to a single vertex and deleting
the remaining vertices and edges of `G` produces a graph containing `H` as a subgraph.
For finite graphs this agrees with the definition of a minor through vertex deletions, edge
deletions and edge contractions. Nonemptiness of `B w` is part of `Connected`.
-/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (B w₁) (B w₂)) ∧
    (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧
    ∀ ⦃w₁ w₂⦄, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ B w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ B w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun _ _ h => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr h,
    fun v => { preconnected := Preconnected.of_subsingleton, nonempty := ⟨⟨v, rfl⟩⟩ },
    fun _ _ h => ⟨_, rfl, _, rfl, h⟩⟩

/-- The empty graph `K_0` is a minor of every graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_zero (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 0)) G :=
  ⟨Fin.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- A minor of a finite graph has at most as many vertices as the graph. In particular a graph
on `n` vertices has no `K_t` minor for `t > n`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.card_le [Fintype V] {H : SimpleGraph W} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    (h : IsMinor H G) : Nat.card W ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  obtain ⟨B, hdisj, hconn, -⟩ := h
  have hne : ∀ w, (B w).Nonempty := fun w =>
    Set.nonempty_coe_sort.mp (hconn w).nonempty
  choose f hf using hne
  rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]
  refine Nat.card_le_card_of_injective f fun w₁ w₂ hw => ?_
  by_contra hne
  exact Set.disjoint_left.mp (hdisj hne) (hf w₁) (hw ▸ hf w₂)

/--
**Hadwiger's conjecture** (1943). Let $t$ be a positive integer. If a finite loopless graph $G$
has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, every graph
with chromatic number at least $t$ contains $K_t$ as a minor, i.e. $\chi(G) \le h(G)$ where
$h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$.

Loops and parallel edges do not affect either side of the statement, so we state it for
simple graphs. The case $t = 0$ is degenerate: every graph has a $K_0$ minor
(see `isMinor_completeGraph_zero`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (h : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) : G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

/--
Hadwiger's conjecture holds for $t \le 6$. The cases $t \le 3$ are elementary, $t = 4$ is due to
Hadwiger [Ha43], $t = 5$ is equivalent to the four color theorem (Wagner, 1937), and $t = 6$ was
proved by Robertson, Seymour and Thomas [RST93].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2.variants.le_six [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : 0 < t) (ht' : t ≤ 6) (h : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2

modeling_decisions: The list entry is terse; the precise formulation is taken from the article lead: 'if G is loopless and has no K_t minor then χ(G) < t'.

Graphs are modelled as Mathlib `SimpleGraph` on a `Fintype` vertex type: the source says 'loopless' (allowing parallel edges), but parallel edges change neither the chromatic number nor the existence of clique minors, so simple graphs lose no generality; finiteness follows the decomposition table (Hadwiger's conjecture is a statement about finite graphs).

/--
**Hadwiger's conjecture** (1943). Let $t$ be a positive integer. If a finite loopless graph $G$
has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, every graph
with chromatic number at least $t$ contains $K_t$ as a minor, i.e. $\chi(G) \le h(G)$ where
$h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$.

Loops and parallel edges do not affect either side of the statement, so we state it for
simple graphs. The case $t = 0$ is degenerate: every graph has a $K_0$ minor
(see `isMinor_completeGraph_zero`).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t)
    (h : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) : G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a finite graph to its complete graph
minors.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

/--
A graph `H` is a minor of a graph `G` if the vertices of `H` can be represented by pairwise
disjoint nonempty connected branch sets in `G`, with every edge of `H` represented by an edge
between the corresponding branch sets.
-/
def IsMinor {W V : Type*} (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : W → Set V,
    (∀ w, (G.induce (branch w)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ ⦃w₁ w₂⦄, w₁ ≠ w₂ → Disjoint (branch w₁) (branch w₂)) ∧
    ∀ ⦃w₁ w₂⦄, H.Adj w₁ w₂ →
      ∃ v₁ ∈ branch w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ branch w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/--
The Hadwiger conjecture: for every finite loopless graph $G$ and every positive integer $t$, if
$G$ has no complete graph $K_t$ as a minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.
Here looplessness is built into `SimpleGraph`, and `IsMinor` uses the branch-set characterization
of graph minors.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 05]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : 0 < t) (hminor : ¬ IsMinor (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin t)) G) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2

Represented K_t as `SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin t)` and graph minors by the standard branch-set characterization.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a graph to its clique minors: if a
loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, every graph $G$
satisfies $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$ (the largest $t$ such
that $K_t$ is a minor of $G$). It is known for $t \le 6$ and open for every $t > 6$.

Mathlib has no notion of graph minor, so this file defines one. A graph $H$ is a minor of a
graph $G$ if $G$ contains pairwise disjoint connected *branch sets* $B_w$, one for each vertex
$w$ of $H$, such that for every edge $w_1 w_2$ of $H$ some edge of $G$ joins $B_{w_1}$ to
$B_{w_2}$. This is equivalent to $H$ being obtained from a subgraph of $G$ by contracting edges.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ha43] Hadwiger, H., *Über eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe*, Vierteljschr.
  Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 88 (1943), 133–142.
- [RST93] Robertson, N., Seymour, P., Thomas, R., *Hadwiger's conjecture for $K_6$-free graphs*,
  Combinatorica 13 (1993), 279–361.
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

open SimpleGraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` says that the graph `H` is a minor of the graph `G`: there are pairwise
disjoint vertex subsets `B w` of `G`, one for each vertex `w` of `H`, each inducing a connected
(in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that whenever `w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H`,
some vertex of `B w₁` is adjacent in `G` to some vertex of `B w₂`.

Contracting each branch set `B w` to a single vertex and deleting the remaining vertices and
edges of `G` yields a graph containing `H` as a spanning subgraph, so this is the usual notion
of a graph minor. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V,
    (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (B w₁) (B w₂)) ∧
    ∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ B w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ B w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/-- A single vertex induces a connected subgraph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
private theorem connected_induce_singleton (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) :
    (G.induce {v}).Connected :=
  haveI : Nonempty ({v} : Set V) := ⟨⟨v, rfl⟩⟩
  ⟨Preconnected.of_subsingleton⟩

/-- Every subgraph of a graph is a minor of it. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {G H : SimpleGraph V} (h : H ≤ G) : IsMinor H G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, connected_induce_singleton G, fun _ _ hvw => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hvw,
    fun v w hvw => ⟨v, rfl, w, rfl, h hvw⟩⟩

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  IsMinor.of_le le_rfl

/-- The empty graph `K₀` is a minor of every graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_fin_zero (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 0)) G :=
  ⟨fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- `K₂` is a minor of a graph if and only if the graph has an edge. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_fin_two_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 2)) G ↔ ∃ v w, G.Adj v w := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨B, -, -, hadj⟩
    obtain ⟨v, -, w, -, hvw⟩ := hadj 0 1 (by decide)
    exact ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
    refine ⟨![{v}, {w}], Fin.forall_fin_two.mpr
      ⟨connected_induce_singleton G v, connected_induce_singleton G w⟩,
      fun i j hij => ?_, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
    · fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.ne, hvw.ne.symm]
    · fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.symm]

/-- A graph with fewer than `t` vertices has no `K_t` minor. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem not_isMinor_completeGraph_of_card_lt [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) {t : ℕ}
    (ht : Fintype.card V < t) : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G := by
  rintro ⟨B, hconn, hdisj, -⟩
  have hne : ∀ i, (B i).Nonempty := fun i =>
    Set.nonempty_coe_sort.mp (hconn i).nonempty
  choose f hf using hne
  have hinj : Function.Injective f := fun i j hij => by
    by_contra hne
    exact Set.disjoint_left.mp (hdisj hne) (hf i) (hij ▸ hf j)
  have := Fintype.card_le_of_injective f hinj
  simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at this
  omega

/-- **Hadwiger conjecture.** If a finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its
chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, $\chi(G) \le h(G)$ for every finite graph
$G$, where $h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$.

Loops play no role here since `SimpleGraph` has none, and multiple edges affect neither the
chromatic number nor the existence of a $K_t$ minor. For $t = 0$ the statement is vacuous, since
$K_0$ is a minor of every graph. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (hG : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

/-- The Hadwiger conjecture holds for $t \le 6$. The cases $t \le 4$ are due to Hadwiger [Ha43],
the case $t = 5$ is equivalent to the four color theorem (Wagner), and the case $t = 6$ was
proved by Robertson, Seymour and Thomas [RST93]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2.variants.le_six [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : t ≤ 6) (hG : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2

The conjecture is stated in the article's lead form (no K_t minor → χ(G) < t) with t : ℕ unrestricted. No hypothesis 1 ≤ t is imposed: for t = 0 the hypothesis '¬ K_0 minor' is false (K_0 is a minor of every graph, proved as a test), so the t = 0 instance is vacuously true and the statement is equivalent to the one restricted to t ≥ 1. The docstring records this.
χ(G) is Mathlib's SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber : ℕ∞, compared with the coercion of t; for finite graphs it is always finite, so the strict inequality is the intended one.

K_t is modelled as completeGraph (Fin t). The Hadwiger number h(G) and the algebraic form χ(G) ≤ h(G) are not defined separately since the table asks for the single Prop; they are mentioned as equivalent in the docstring only.
IsMinor requires an edge between branch sets only for edges of H (not 'iff'), which is the standard convention (Diestel's MH) and gives the same minor relation since edge deletion is allowed.

An additional @[category research solved] variant hadwiger_conjecture_2.variants.le_six records the known cases t ≤ 6 (Hadwiger, Wagner/four colour theorem, Robertson–Seymour–Thomas), following repository practice; it is not one of the table's slots.
A private helper connected_induce_singleton (a singleton induces a connected subgraph) is tagged @[category API] as is done for helpers elsewhere in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)

The Hadwiger conjecture relates the chromatic number of a graph to its clique minors: if a
loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, every graph with
chromatic number at least $k$ contains $k$ pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs, each pair of
which is joined by an edge, so that contracting these subgraphs yields $K_k$ as a minor.

The conjecture was made by Hadwiger in 1943 [Ha43]. It is known for $t \le 6$; the case $t = 5$
is equivalent to the four color theorem (Wagner, 1937) and the case $t = 6$ was proved by
Robertson, Seymour and Thomas [RST93]. It is open for every $t > 6$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
- [Ha43] Hadwiger, H., *Über eine Klassifikation der Streckenkomplexe*. Vierteljschr.
  Naturforsch. Ges. Zürich 88 (1943), 133–142.
- [RST93] Robertson, N., Seymour, P. and Thomas, R., *Hadwiger's conjecture for $K_6$-free
  graphs*. Combinatorica 13 (1993), 279–361.
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

open SimpleGraph

variable {V W : Type*}

/--
A graph `H` is a *minor* of a graph `G` if `G` contains a model of `H`: a family of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `f w` of `G` (the *branch sets*), one for each vertex `w` of `H`, such that
every branch set induces a connected (in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, and whenever
`w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H` some vertex of `f w₁` is adjacent in `G` to some vertex of
`f w₂`.

Equivalently, `H` is isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of `G` by contracting edges
(each branch set is contracted to a single vertex).
-/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (f w)).Connected) ∧
    (Pairwise fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (f w₁) (f w₂)) ∧
    ∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ f w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ f w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself: take every branch set to be a single vertex. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun v => by simp, fun v w hvw => by simpa,
    fun v w h => ⟨v, rfl, w, rfl, h⟩⟩

/-- A minor of a subgraph of `G` is a minor of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {K : SimpleGraph W} {G G' : SimpleGraph V} (hG : G ≤ G')
    (h : IsMinor K G) : IsMinor K G' := by
  obtain ⟨f, hconn, hdisj, hadj⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, fun w => (hconn w).mono fun _ _ h => hG h, hdisj, fun w₁ w₂ hw => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hv⟩ := hadj w₁ w₂ hw
  exact ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hG hv⟩

/--
The complete graph on zero vertices is a minor of every graph. In particular the case $t = 0$
of the Hadwiger conjecture holds vacuously.
-/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_zero (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 0)) G :=
  ⟨Fin.elim0, fun w => w.elim0, fun w => w.elim0, fun w => w.elim0⟩

/-- A graph has a $K_1$ minor if and only if it has a vertex. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_one_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 1)) G ↔ Nonempty V := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, hf, -, -⟩
    obtain ⟨⟨v, -⟩⟩ := (hf 0).nonempty
    exact ⟨v⟩
  · rintro ⟨v⟩
    refine ⟨fun _ => {v}, fun _ => by simp, fun i j hij => (hij (Subsingleton.elim i j)).elim,
      fun i j h => ?_⟩
    exact absurd (Subsingleton.elim i j) h.ne

/-- A graph has a $K_2$ minor if and only if it has an edge. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_completeGraph_two_iff (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin 2)) G ↔ ∃ v w, G.Adj v w := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨f, -, -, hadj⟩
    obtain ⟨v, -, w, -, hvw⟩ := hadj 0 1 (by decide)
    exact ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, w, hvw⟩
    refine ⟨![{v}, {w}], fun i => by fin_cases i <;> simp, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i j hij
      fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.ne, hvw.ne.symm]
    · intro i j hij
      fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp_all [hvw.symm]

/--
**Hadwiger conjecture.** If a finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic
number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, if every proper coloring of $G$ uses at least $k$
colors, then $G$ contains $k$ pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs such that each pair of them
is joined by an edge, i.e. $G$ has a $K_k$ minor. In algebraic form: $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where
$h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$ (the largest $k$ such that $K_k$ is a minor of $G$).

A simple graph is loopless by definition. No restriction on $t$ is needed: $K_0$ is a minor of
every graph, so the case $t = 0$ is vacuous.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (hG : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) : G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

/--
The Hadwiger conjecture is known to be true for $t \le 6$. The case $t = 5$ is equivalent to the
four color theorem (Wagner, 1937) and the case $t = 6$ was proved by Robertson, Seymour and
Thomas [RST93], also using the four color theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2.variants.le_six [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : t ≤ 6) (hG : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) : G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2

Formalized in exactly that direction with a strict inequality; the equivalent forms (contrapositive, χ(G) ≤ h(G)) are only described in the docstring, not stated separately, per the decomposition table.

Graphs are Mathlib SimpleGraphs, which are loopless by definition. Wikipedia's 'loopless' allows multigraphs with parallel edges, but parallel edges change neither the chromatic number nor the existence of a K_t minor, so restricting to simple graphs loses nothing.
Finiteness is imposed via [Fintype V] on a universe-polymorphic vertex type, as the decomposition notes require and as is standard in the repository's graph files.

No hypothesis 0 < t is included. With the branch-set definition, K_0 is a minor of every graph (proved as isMinor_completeGraph_zero), so the t = 0 instance of the theorem is vacuous and the statement is logically equivalent to the one restricted to t ≥ 1 (Wikipedia's range 1 ≤ t ≤ 6 for the known cases). This is explained in the theorem docstring.

Minor containment is defined with 'at least one edge between adjacent branch sets' (rather than 'iff'), which is the correct ∃-characterization of 'H is a minor of G' since minors allow edge deletion; for H = K_t the two coincide anyway.

The bespoke definition lives in the problem file because the sandbox permits writing only candidate.lean; in a real PR it would arguably belong in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/ as a reusable definition (with its API lemmas), and a reviewer may wish to move it.

An additional research-solved variant hadwiger_conjecture_2.variants.le_six records the known cases t ≤ 6 (Wagner 1937 for t = 5 via the four color theorem; Robertson–Seymour–Thomas 1993 for t = 6), with a sorry proof body as the repo allows for informally established results.

new_definitions.name: HadwigerConjecture2.IsMinor
new_definitions.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has any notion of a graph minor (only Matroid.IsMinor exists). Defined via the standard model/branch-set characterization: H is a minor of G iff there is a family f : W → Set V of pairwise disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a connected (hence nonempty) subgraph of G, with an edge of G between f w₁ and f w₂ whenever w₁ ~ w₂ in H. This is equivalent (Diestel, Ch. 1.7) to H being isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of G by edge contractions. Five short proved API lemmas exercise it: reflexivity, monotonicity in G, K_0 is a minor of everything, K_1 minor ↔ Nonempty V, K_2 minor ↔ G has an edge.

hadwiger_conjecture_2.why: Stated as: for every finite simple graph G (on a Fintype vertex type) and every t : ℕ, if the complete graph on Fin t is not a minor of G then G.chromaticNumber < t (in ℕ∞). Mathlib has no notion of graph minor, so a bespoke branch-set (model) definition IsMinor was added in the problem file; the K_t instance is literally Wikipedia's 'k disjoint connected subgraphs, each pair joined by an edge'.

statement_blocks.hadwiger_conjecture_2:
/--
**Hadwiger conjecture.** If a finite loopless graph $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic
number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$. Equivalently, if every proper coloring of $G$ uses at least $k$
colors, then $G$ contains $k$ pairwise disjoint connected subgraphs such that each pair of them
is joined by an edge, i.e. $G$ has a $K_k$ minor. In algebraic form: $\chi(G) \le h(G)$, where
$h(G)$ is the Hadwiger number of $G$ (the largest $k$ such that $K_k$ is a minor of $G$).

A simple graph is loopless by definition. No restriction on $t$ is needed: $K_0$ is a minor of
every graph, so the case $t = 0$ is vacuous.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (hG : ¬ IsMinor (completeGraph (Fin t)) G) : G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28graph_theory%29)
-/

namespace HadwigerConjecture2

/--
A simple graph `G` has a complete graph on `t` vertices as a minor if it has `t` nonempty,
pairwise disjoint connected branch sets, with an edge joining every two distinct branch sets.
-/
def HasCompleteMinor {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ branch : Fin t → Set V,
    (∀ i, (G.induce (branch i)).Connected) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (branch i) (branch j)) ∧
    ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∃ u ∈ branch i, ∃ v ∈ branch j, G.Adj u v

/--
The Hadwiger conjecture: for every finite loopless simple graph $G$ and every positive integer
$t$, if $G$ has no $K_t$ minor, then its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G) < t$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture_2 {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ)
    (ht : 1 ≤ t) (hminor : ¬ HasCompleteMinor G t) :
    G.chromaticNumber < t := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture2
modeling_decisions: The terse list entry was expanded using the cited Hadwiger-conjecture article: for every finite simple graph G and positive natural number t, absence of a K_t minor implies χ(G) < t.
Finite loopless undirected graphs are represented by `SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]`; looplessness and symmetry are built into `SimpleGraph`.

A K_t minor is represented by t pairwise disjoint connected branch sets with an edge between every two distinct branch sets. This is the standard branch-set characterization of a complete-graph minor and implicitly permits deletion of unused vertices and edges.
Positivity is stated explicitly as `1 ≤ t`. The bespoke predicate still has the mathematically expected degenerate behavior that every graph has a K_0 minor.
Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber` is `ℕ∞`-valued, so the conclusion elaborates as `G.chromaticNumber < (t : ℕ∞)`. For finite graphs this is the usual finite chromatic number comparison.
